one_liner: TileLang-built fused CUDA kernels for Gated DeltaNet chunked prefill; about 2x faster forward and 2.5-3x faster backward than FLA Triton.
what_it_does: FlashQLA implements the forward and backward passes of the Gated DeltaNet (GDN) chunked-prefill linear-attention layer used by Qwen3.5/3.6 (and Qwen3-Next) for PyTorch on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs. Its high-level entry point chunk_gated_delta_rule(q, k, v, g, beta, scale, initial_state, output_final_state, cu_seqlens) mirrors the flash-linear-attention (FLA) signature and is an autograd Function, with separate _fwd/_bwd calls for frameworks that manage their own graph. Since v0.1.2 it is also a backend for FLA's own GDN op, so FLA users can get it through the standard FLA API.
how_it_is_fast: Instead of FLA's chain of separate Triton kernels, it fuses gate, decay and matmul stages into a few warp-specialized TileLang kernels that overlap TMA data movement, Tensor Core and CUDA Core work, with separate Hopper (sm90), Blackwell (sm100/103) and sm120 code paths. An algebraic reformulation of the GDN chunked forward/backward cuts Tensor Core, CUDA Core and SFU (exp) work. When heads per GPU are few (high TP) or sequences are long, it uses the exponential decay of the gate to split one sequence across SMs (gate-driven intra-card context parallelism), which is why the biggest gains are at TP8 with long single sequences.
when_to_use: Training or prefill of GDN-based models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Qwen3-Next style linear-attention layers) at head dim 128 in bf16 on H100/H200, B200/GB200 or RTX 50-series
Long single sequences with few heads per GPU (tensor parallel TP4-TP8): H200 1x32768 at TP8 forward 0.348 ms vs FLA 1.019 ms and FlashInfer 1.645 ms
Backward pass / pretraining: 32 backward shapes on H200 run 1.38x to 5.47x faster than FLA (geometric mean about 2.6x); FlashInfer has no GDN backward to compare
Already on FLA: switch via FLA's FlashQLA backend or the same-signature chunk_gated_delta_rule without changing model code
when_not_to_use: Inference serving with many short varlen sequences and FlashInfer available: FlashInfer's GDN prefill beats FlashQLA in 56 of 171 H200 forward rows and 85 of 171 GB200 rows (down to 0.48x), so FlashQLA is roughly at parity there
Decode / token-by-token generation or MTP: only chunked prefill is implemented (decode and MTP kernels are an open feature request, issue #11)
Ampere, Ada, AMD or Ascend hardware: import raises ValueError on anything other than sm90, sm100, sm103, sm120 or sm121

Packed varlen batches whose segments are shorter than one 64-token chunk on B200: issue #43 measured L32 at 4.4x and L63 at 7.7x slower than padding to L64 (incomplete chunks fall back from TMA to guarded elementwise loads)
RTX 5090 / sm120 varlen workloads in production: issue #35 (open) reports four forward tests on varlen/padding configs with relative errors of 1e16-1e25

integration.dependencies: PyTorch >= 2.8, TileLang >= 0.1.12 (kernels compiled through TileLang), CUDA 12.8+; FLA and FlashInfer only for benchmarks and tests
integration.platforms: NVIDIA sm90 (Hopper), sm100/sm103 (B200, GB200, B300), sm120/sm121 (RTX 50-series, DGX Spark GB10); Linux; no CPU or AMD path
integration.thread_safety: not documented (module-level tensor_cache with mutable shared entries and no lock)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same argument layout as FLA's chunk_gated_delta_rule and selectable as an FLA backend, but bf16/fp16 only, head_first=True unsupported, B must be 1 when cu_seqlens is given, and inter+intra CP is rejected on sm120

gotchas: The kernel set is chosen at import time from tilelang's detected compute capability, so a process with mixed GPU generations or no supported GPU fails on import

Numerics differ from FLA: tests check a 2% relative error against an fp64 reference; issue #15 (closed, no explanation shown) reported max abs diff 0.047 vs FLA Triton that flipped greedy tokens on 2 of 3 prompts. Validate end-to-end outputs before switching inference

Issue #23 (B200 integrator) found heap-corruption risks from an id()-keyed tensor cache and from zero-length cu_seqlens segments; the current utils/index.py keys on object identity instead, but check zero-length segments on your version

Benchmarks and tests use bf16 inputs; open issue #38 reports NaNs in fp16 forward beyond 32k tokens (reporter's H100/CUDA 12.4/PyTorch 2.4 setup is below the stated requirements, so unconfirmed). Prefer bf16
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FlashQLA for GDN (gated delta rule) layers, training or long-context prefill; pick FlashKDA for Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers, and FlashInfer's GDN prefill for batched short-sequence serving where it is as fast or faster. FlashAttention-3 and SageAttention cover softmax attention, not linear attention.
verified_claims_summary: First-party per-shape CUDA-graph timings (10 warmup, 100 repeats, bf16, d=128) from the public benchmark/bench_gated_delta_rule.py on H200 (torch 2.8.0+cu128, FLA 0.5.1, FlashInfer 0.6.13, TileLang 0.1.12) and GB200: forward 1.18-3.32x vs FLA Triton on H200 (geometric mean about 2.1x) and 1.07-3.58x on GB200, but only roughly at parity with FlashInfer's GDN prefill (as low as 0.48x on GB200 small-batch varlen); backward 1.38-5.47x (H200) and 1.94-6.44x (GB200) vs FLA. Host CPU and compiler flags are not stated.
status_note: Very active Qwen/Alibaba project (v0.1.3, last commit 2026-09-30, 716 stars), MIT-licensed and pip-installable as flash-qla; young (first release April 2026) with open correctness issues on sm120 varlen.
